name: collapsible-row
title: Collapsible app bar (priorities)
summary: An Inbox app bar shown at five widths: a collapsibleRow drops its children by collapsiblePriority as space runs out (the unread Badge first, then share, then search), keeps the unprioritized title and overflow menu longest, and a weighted spacer keeps the IconButtons pushed to the end at every width.
prompt: An app bar (title "Inbox", a "12 new" chip, search, share and an overflow menu) that drops its least important items as it narrows: the chip first, then share, then search; the title and the overflow menu stay. Show it at 328, 240, 200, 152 and 112 dp.
hand_built: The bar is a collapsibleRow written out, not a TopBar, because dropping actions by collapsiblePriority is the lesson and TopBar has no priorities; its actions are library IconButtons and the unread count a Badge.
teaches: Let a collapsibleRow decide what fits: children are kept in priority order (highest first) and dropped from the lowest priority up once the next one no longer fits
Rank children with collapsiblePriority {orientation: horizontal, priority: N}; leave the must-stay ones (title, overflow menu) without a priority, which counts as the highest
Push the actions to the end with an unprioritized weighted spacer: it takes only the space left over and never causes a drop
Size the container, not the collapsibleRow, when its children include a weight: give the row fillMaxWidth inside a box of the width you want
Give a component call a priority by wrapping it in a box that carries the collapsiblePriority modifier: a call such as IconButton or Badge takes no modifiers of its own
pitfalls: Unprioritized children all tie at the top and keep document order among themselves: at 112 dp the title (first) stays and the overflow menu (last) goes

The fit test adds up the children's widths only, not spacedBy: with spacedBy 10 a 225 dp row keeps 220 dp of children and overflows by 20 dp. Build gaps into the children's own widths (as the 76 dp title box does) instead
Priorities compare by the integer part of their difference, so values less than 1 apart tie and 2, 2.5, 3 is not a consistent order (at 250 dp Java keeps 3 and 2 and drops 2.5): use whole numbers
Dropping stops at the first child that does not fit: a lower-priority child that is narrow enough to fit is dropped too, so give similar-sized items adjacent priorities

Don't give the weighted spacer a priority: it is then ranked and dropped like any other child as soon as space is short (at 200 dp a priority-0 spacer went while 40 dp were still free), and the remaining items re-centre instead of staying at the ends
A child with a weight makes a row or collapsibleRow ignore its own width modifier and fill its parent (Java, matched by both players): wrap it in a box of the width you want

A nested collapsibleRow is measured against the width left after its earlier siblings in document order, not after the higher-priority ones, so its own drops can interleave oddly with the parent's (an inner label kept while a higher-priority sibling goes, then the reverse a few dp narrower)
A demo of fixed widths overflows a narrower host if one of them is as wide as the header's content area: make the widest one fillMaxWidth so it becomes the live, resizing case

snippets.note: the whole bar: collapsibleRow with title, Badge, spacer and three IconButtons
the Badge's wrapper box, collapsiblePriority 1: the first to go
the search IconButton's wrapper box, priority 3: the last action to go
unprioritized weighted spacer: takes the leftover width only

check.describe: Five bars: the first is full width (328 dp at 360) and shows everything; 240 dp drops the "12 new" Badge; 200 dp also drops share; 152 dp also drops search (title and overflow menu left); 112 dp keeps only the title. The IconButtons (48 dp targets) stay right-aligned in every bar. In mono the bars are outlined so their widths stay visible. Resized: the full-width bar is the live one — at 300 wide (268 dp) it has already dropped the Badge, at 540 it shows everything with the icons at the far end; the four fixed-width bars below are unchanged.
